'''''Ctenanthe''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Marantaceae]] described as a genus in 1884.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/92798#page/147/mode/1up Eichler, August Wilhelm. 1884.  Abhandlungen der Königlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin 1884: 81-84] descriptions in Latin, commentary in German</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40017693 Tropicos, ''Ctenanthe'' Eichler ]</ref> They are [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]]s, [[native plant|native]] to [[Central America|Central]] and [[South America]] (primarily [[Brazil]]).<ref name=b>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=235147 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>Forzza, R. C. 2010. Lista de espécies Flora do Brasil {{cite web|url=http://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/2010 |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2015-08-20 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906080403/http://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/2010/ |archivedate=2015-09-06 }}. Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro</ref> They are grown for their attractive, often variegated foliage. They are frost [[Hardiness (plants)|tender]], requiring a minimum temperature of {{convert|13|C|0|abbr=on}}.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

== Species ==

The genus has the following species:<ref name=b/>
{{columns-list|colwidth=30em|
* ''[[Ctenanthe amabilis]]'' - Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe amphiandina]]'' - Ecuador, Peru, NW Brazil, Colombia, Bolivia<ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/19700549?tab=specimens Tropicos, specimens for ''Ctenanthe amphiandina'' L. Andersson ]</ref>
* ''[[Ctenanthe burle-marxii]]'' - [[Espírito Santo]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe casupoides]]'' - E + S Brazil, [[Misiones Province|Misiones]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe compressa]]'' - Venezuela, Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe dasycarpa]]'' - Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia
* ''[[Ctenanthe ericae]]'' - SE Colombia, Ecuador, [[Acre (state)|Acre]], [[Rondônia]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe glabra]]'' - Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe kummerana]]'' - [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe lanceolata]]'' - S + SE Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe lubbersiana]]'' - [[Minas Gerais]], [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe marantifolia]]'' - SE Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe muelleri]]'' - S + SE Brazil
* ''[[Ctenanthe oppenheimiana]]'' - [[Bahia]]
* ''[[Ctenanthe setosa]]'' - S + E Brazil
}}

== Awards ==

The [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]] has been awarded to the following:
*''Ctenanthe amabilis''<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/77290/Ctenanthe-amabilis/Details | title = ''Ctenanthe amabilis'' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 5 May 2020}}</ref>
*''Ctenanthe lubbersiana'' <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/30925/Ctenanthe-lubbersiana/Details | title = ''Ctenanthe lubbersiana'' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 5 May 2020}}</ref> (common name: bamburanta), which grows to {{convert|2|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} and bears large, oval leaves up to {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, heavily striped and mottled with yellow
*''Ctenanthe oppenheimiana'' 'Tricolor' <ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/30926/Ctenanthe-oppenheimiana-Tricolor/Details | title = ''Ctenanthe oppenheimiana'' 'Tricolor' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 5 May 2020}}</ref> (common name "never-never plant"), which grows to {{convert|2|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} with narrow, oval leaves up to {{convert|40|cm|0|abbr=on}} long with V-shaped silver patterns above and maroon below.<ref>Idárraga-Piedrahita, A., R. D. C. Ortiz, R. Callejas Posada & M. Merello. (eds.) 2011. Flora de Antioquia: Catálogo de las Plantas Vasculares 2: 9–939. Universidad de Antioquia, Medellín</ref>
